A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DiMA study. The main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A–F are readable and can be matched despite additions and repagination.

before.justification: V2 reports original protein-generation experiments, architectural ablations, conditional-generation benchmarks and biological annotation analyses in Section 3 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds sampling sensitivity results, noisy-representation reconstruction analyses and a PLAID comparison.

M1.justification: The encoder–denoiser–decoder architecture, training objective and conditional-generation mechanisms are retained. V3 clarifies normalization and decoder fine-tuning, documents self-conditioning-weight sensitivity, and renames sd-10 to tan-10; these do not establish a change to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions retain SwissProt, AFDBv4-90, the eight protein families, sequence infilling, motif scaffolding and fold-conditioned benchmarks. The added sampling and noise analyses examine existing protein representations without establishing additional dataset or application coverage.

E2.justification: V3 adds PLAID-100M to the pretrained-model comparison in Section 3.5, Figure 3 and Table 8. Existing comparators remain, including those in the conditional-generation and structure-generation experiments.

E3.justification: Section 3.5 changes the reported sampling protocol from authors’ recommended settings for all models to temperature/top-p grid searches for ProGen2 and ProLLAMA. Their scores remain unchanged, so rerunning is not established. New analyses include a self-conditioning-weight sweep from 0.6 to 1.3 at 2,000 sampling steps and CHEAP reconstruction across noise levels.

E4.justification: New Appendices C.4–C.5 add self-conditioning-strength sensitivity and CHEAP sequence/structure robustness analyses, and extend sampling-step analysis with clustering diversity and novelty. V2’s existing sampling-step study remains as v3 Figure 15. The noise-schedule reconstruction-loss curves are also revised.

E5.justification: Existing plus/minus pLDDT summaries in Appendix B.2 are retained. V3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests; the new sensitivity plots have no uncertainty bands or error bars.

E6.justification: Table 8 adds PLAID-100M results, including pLDDT 53.5 and CD0.5 1.000, while existing table scores remain unchanged. Reconstruction-loss curves change between v2 Figure 1 and v3 Figure 2. New Figures 11–14 report sampling trade-offs and noise-reconstruction results, including approximately 100% sequence accuracy and structural RMSD below 0.2 Å at t = 0.05.

T1.justification: The diffusion objective, noise-schedule equation and evaluation-metric definitions are retained. Appendix C.5 supplies heuristic motivation and empirical illustrations rather than a new formal assumption, theorem, proof or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list retain the claims of encoder generality, efficient generation, competitive quality/diversity and adaptation to conditional tasks. The rewritten conclusion emphasizes capabilities already claimed in v2 rather than expanding their scientific scope.

C2.justification: V3 adds explanations connecting decoder fine-tuning to embedding perturbation sensitivity and low-noise reconstruction robustness to allocating training effort toward harder noise levels. It also expands the discussion of continuous versus discrete diffusion and interprets sampling controls through quality, diversity and novelty trade-offs.

D1.justification: V3 adds a DiMA code-release link, specifies training-data statistics for per-component normalization, explicitly states d = 10, and describes fine-tuning CHEAP/SaProt decoders. These are additional disclosures. The new grid-search statement does not provide search ranges or selected settings.

R1.justification: V3 expands positioning against discrete diffusion and introduces PLAID into the comparison discussion. The reference list is unchanged, and the new PLAID citation and an additional Appendix D citation appear as unresolved question marks.

P1.justification: V3 expands the introduction and method motivation, clarifies technical passages, converts the ablation list into prose, adds Appendices C.4–C.5 and rewrites the conclusion. The overall section organization and most text remain intact; title capitalization and publication information also change.

P2.justification: V3 adds the framework overview in Figure 1 and four analysis figures in Appendix C. It restyles the noise-schedule plot and pretrained-model comparison, adds PLAID to the latter and Table 8, and repositions some main-text displays. Most existing figures and table layouts are retained.

improvement.justification: The framework overview, clearer implementation disclosures, code-release link and new sensitivity analyses improve accessibility and support for sampling choices. These are limited gains around largely retained evidence and claims. Unresolved citations and the mismatch between Section 3.5’s tuning statement and Appendix E.4’s unchanged recommended-settings description limit the improvement in reproducibility.
